chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Abbad ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from a man, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who becomes ill during the month of Ramadan, then recovers afterwards, but delays making up the missed days for a year, or less than that, or more. What is incumbent upon him in that case? He said: 'I like for him to hasten the fasting. If he delays it, there is nothing upon him (in terms of compensation).'

Indeed, this is also based on what we mentioned previously, that whenever he delays it without being negligent, and intends to fast, there is nothing upon him from the charity (kaffarah), and only making up the days is incumbent upon him, according to what the Quran encompasses.

Allah, the Exalted, said: 'The month of Ramadan in which the Quran was revealed, a guidance for the people and clear proofs of guidance and the criterion. So whoever witnesses the month, let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days.'

So He made it obligatory upon whoever witnesses the month of Ramadan to fast it, and upon whoever is traveling or ill to fast an equal number of other days. And this is not contradictory to what we said first, and praise is to Allah alone.

key_terms.الصَّدَقَةُ: Charity or expiation (kaffarah) in this context
key_terms.الْقَضَاءُ: Making up missed obligatory acts, specifically fasting days
key_terms.الْمُتَهَاوِنٌ: One who is negligent or careless
key_terms.عِدَّةٌ مِنْ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَ: An equal number of other days

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for delaying Ramadan makeup fasts for more than a year without a valid excuse?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), clarifying that delaying the makeup of Ramadan fasts due to illness or valid excuse incurs no expiation (kaffarah), only the missed days themselves. This ruling is grounded in the Quranic principle of ease, distinguishing between the obligation of *qada* and the penalty for negligence. The text explicitly links this legal derivation to the verse in Surah Al-Baqarah, emphasizing that the Quranic mandate for the sick to fast 'a number of other days' applies without additional penalty unless negligence is proven.
